# Erry Mobility — Forward, your way.

Erry Mobility is an independent, student-led biomedical engineering education project. It explores everyday movement, accessible design and how to compare changes to a typing setup. Erry’s lived-experience brief and design direction informed the project. AI tools assisted with implementation, illustrations and verification.

- [Public website](https://hteteaindraykyaw296.github.io/Erry-Mobility-/)
- [Project brief](../project-brief.md)
- [Project scope and limitations](https://hteteaindraykyaw296.github.io/Erry-Mobility-/scope.html)

## Biomedical Engineering Design and Evaluation

The Engineering Lab includes a planar reach calculator and worked examples for keyguard clearance and static support. The Typing Setup Lab compares one documented change at a time and records pause-adjusted task completion time, final text errors and optional comfort.

The release candidate passed 23 numerical and data-format tests, 12 targeted browser reach checks and a separate Chromium regression suite. Tested examples included the 200 mm versus 150 mm reach comparison, edit-distance cases, a two-pause 1.25 s timing scenario, repeat-trial summaries and exact CSV output. The production smoke test checked the mobile homepage, reach calculator, typing and reload, motor illustration and journal page.

These checks establish specific software behaviours. The illustrations and device concepts remain educational. The project has no participant outcomes, clinical validation or manufactured keyguard fit evidence.

Journal data stays in the current browser. Export a backup before changing browsers or website origins. Photograph and software credits appear alongside the assets or in the site files.
